title: rewind.py CLI: partition + watermark rollback across 5 layers
objective: New module etl4/orchestration/rewind.py per architecture section 7. CLI rewinds one layer (or all) to before a specified ym range: deletes partitions + resets pipeline_watermarks so the next pipeline invocation re-does only the rewound months. Layers: vault, marts, sink, matrix, eval_mart, all. --yes required for --layer all. --dry-run prints the plan and exits 0 without touching anything.
depends_on: T-01B (pipeline_runs.ym UNIQUE + eval_results ON DELETE CASCADE, DONE)
unblocks: T-22 (run_e2e pre-flight drift check can suggest 'rewind --layer vault' in its error message)
T-27 (functional-tester rewind E2E: delete ym, verify partitions + watermark roll back)

files_changed.note: CLI (argparse main) + five layer functions (rewind_vault, rewind_marts, rewind_sink, rewind_matrix, rewind_eval_mart) + rewind_all chain + helpers (months_between, month_minus_one, _reset_layer_watermark, _dir_size, _validate_ym). Downstream-first chain order for --layer all: eval_mart -> matrix -> sink -> marts -> vault (architecture section 7 rationale 'upstream rebuilds never leave orphans', overrides dispatch's forward-order listing).

End-to-end smoke: scratch dir with 2 ym partitions ('hub_flight' table; 2022-01 + 2022-02); snapshots & restores production ('vault','hub_flight') watermark row; invokes rewind.rewind_vault('2022-02','2022-02', root=<scratch>); asserts 2022-02 deleted, 2022-01 survives, watermark rolled 2022-02 -> 2022-01. Also drives the three CLI acceptance items (dry-run, --yes gate, --yes --dry-run chain plan) via subprocess.

contract_deviations: Task spec said 'all: chain vault -> marts -> sink -> matrix -> eval_mart' (forward pipeline order). Architecture section 7 explicitly says 'downstream-first deletion so upstream rebuilds never leave orphans'. Dispatch binds section 7. Implemented downstream-first: eval_mart -> matrix -> sink -> marts -> vault. Downstream-first is safer under mid-rewind crash: deleting vault before sink would leave sink rows with no vault source for several seconds; deleting sink before vault leaves vault intact above a transiently empty sink, which the sink will re-populate on next run. Flagged for data-engineer review.
spec_gaps_resolved: Spec silent on eval_mart rewind semantics beyond 'delete+rebuild; reset watermark'. fact_experiment_result is latest-per-cell (architecture section 4.5, MAX(ym) over pipeline_runs); dropping rows for a ym range would wipe cells whose latest observation lives OUTSIDE the range. Implemented: rewind_eval_mart() ONLY resets the layer='eval_mart' watermark and prints an explicit note that stage_eval_mart must be re-run after the matrix rewind to resettle MAX(ym). The eval_mart rebuild is therefore the subsequent stage_eval_mart invocation, not a DELETE inside rewind.

Spec silent on the filesystem-vs-Postgres atomicity order for vault + marts. Implemented: delete filesystem FIRST, then open psycopg txn and update watermark in that txn. A crash between the two leaves the watermark AHEAD of what is on disk; the T-22 drift check catches that and the operator reruns rewind. The reverse order (watermark first, then filesystem) would leave the watermark BEHIND real data and the builder would silently skip rebuild -- data missing forever.

Spec silent on which non-partitioned sink table is touched. Implemented: only fact_trajectory_enriched. dim_aircraft is non-partitioned (airframes persist across months) and its sink watermark is not reset here either. The _reset_layer_watermark(table_filter=...) hook enforces that so a future dim table added under layer='sink' does not get rolled back by accident.

Spec silent on the exact watermark rollback condition. Implemented: UPDATE ... WHERE layer=X AND last_ym >= from_ym. The '>=' guard means rewinding to a ym that is already before the current watermark is a no-op (no forward-roll) -- matches architecture section 7's sketch, and prevents the second-of-two 'rewind 2022-02' invocations from mistakenly bumping the watermark to the pre-month of 2022-02 when it has already been rolled past.

Spec silent on dry-run behavior under a pre-migration DB (fact_trajectory_enriched.ym column may not exist yet). Implemented: dry-run ONLY catches psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn in rewind_sink and logs a note that the section 6.1 migration must run first; non-dry-run never swallows that error -- a missing column fails loudly in a real run. Without this fallback, --layer all --dry-run on a pre-migration DB crashes before marts/vault plans are printed.
risks: AC-4 chain plan on this test DB shows 'fact_trajectory_enriched.ym column missing' because the section 6.1 Postgres schema migration (ADD COLUMN ym + backfill + NOT NULL + index) has not been applied. T-01B landed pipeline_runs.ym but not fact_trajectory_enriched.ym. On a production DB with that migration applied, rewind_sink's dry-run will print 'would delete: fact_trajectory_enriched rows=N' as the architecture specifies. No code change needed in rewind.py once the schema migration lands.

rewind_marts silently succeeds when no marts partitions exist yet (fact_flight / fact_trajectory_enriched trees under data/gold/marts/ are produced by T-14 which is not yet done). Current behaviour prints 'total: 0 dirs, 0 bytes' and resets the watermark -- which is correct for an empty tree, but means an operator who misspells a layer name (e.g. 'mart' vs 'marts') will see a successful no-op rather than an error. Mitigation: argparse choices=LAYERS already prevents the misspelling case; an unknown layer exits non-zero from argparse before the function runs.

rewind_matrix DELETEs pipeline_runs for calendar ym; it does NOT touch SYN-<hex> synthetic sentinel rows. An operator who wants to rewind the synthetic cell must do so manually (DELETE FROM pipeline_runs WHERE ym='SYN-002A'; cascade handles eval_results). Flagged as follow-up because the architecture is silent on synthetic rewind.

No subprocess-level test that rewind_vault / rewind_marts filesystem delete succeeds on Windows with a ReadOnly flag or an open file handle. shutil.rmtree will raise on either. The smoke test runs on tempdir with no concurrent readers; production usage during an active vault build would likely hit this and crash. Mitigation is procedural: operators run rewind only when the pipeline is idle. The task scope does not include retry-on-WindowsError.
notes: Implementation details: (a) Filesystem order: delete partitions BEFORE watermark reset (fails toward 'watermark ahead of disk' which T-22 drift-catches, not toward 'data missing forever'). (b) Watermark rollback uses UPDATE ... WHERE last_ym >= from_ym so re-runs do not forward-roll a watermark. (c) --layer all chain is downstream-first (eval_mart -> matrix -> sink -> marts -> vault) per architecture section 7 rationale, overriding the dispatch's forward-order listing. (d) rewind_eval_mart does NOT delete fact_experiment_result rows because those are latest-per-cell (MAX(ym)); the rebuild path is a subsequent stage_eval_mart invocation after matrix rewind. (e) Dry-run on sink layer tolerates the pre-migration state (no ym column) so AC-4 full-chain plan prints on this test DB; production dry-run after the section 6.1 migration lands prints row counts normally. (f) Unused helper psycopg import is retained (psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn) and does not shadow the builtin set.
